subject: maths
question: Three horses are tied at three vertices of a triangular field, each with a 7 m long rope. What is the total area grazed by the horses?
solution:
Given:

Three horses are tied at three vertices of a triangular field, each with a 7 m long rope.

Concept used:

Area of a sector θ° of a circle = π × R2 × θ/360

(R is the radius of the circle)

π = 22/7

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92b42fd9b4f6324a14af59cab3d28f891ffcd3e4fd2db5b4c1f3c05b4679fb1f.png] 

Here, the horses tied at vertices A, B, and C will gaze at the field in the form of a sector of a circle that has a radius of 7 m. 

Let the angles at vertices A, B, and C be θ₁, θ₂, and θ₃ respectively.

According to the question,

(θ1 + θ2 + θ3) = 180° ....(1)

Area gazed by the horse at vertex A = π × 7² × θ1/360

Area gazed by the horse at vertex B = π × 72 × θ2/360

Area gazed by the horse at vertex C = π × 72 × θ3/360

Now, the total area gazed

⇒ π × 72 × θ1/360 + π × 72 × θ2/360 + π × 72 × θ3/360

⇒ π × 49 × (θ1 + θ₂ + θ₃)/360

⇒ 154 × 180/360 (From 1)

⇒ 154/2

⇒ 77 m²

∴ The total gazed area by the horses is 77 m².
